about: Editor spec §42, problem_codes: the stable code of every problem the document profile reader raises (ProfileError), the same from the JavaScript and the Python libraries, and given as the Language Server Protocol diagnostic's code, so a problem's message and fix can be translated and looked up. A code is GN and three digits, numbered in groups by area: 1xx the header and tokens, 2xx the grammar and its values, 3xx the store, 4xx change sets, 5xx writing standard GQL, 6xx the limits on reading. 7xx is the editor's drawing reader's, in packages/core/src/drawing-problem-codes.json, so this table never takes it. A code is never reused and never renumbered: a problem that goes keeps its code retired, and a new one takes the next free number in its group. message and fix are templates, each {name} standing for a part the problem fills in; section is the spec § the rule comes from, or null; the words themselves never cite it (NEURO-4). libraries says which library raises it: js, py or both. Every raise site passes its code as a literal; packages/graph-spec/test/problem-codes.test.mjs and python/graph_spec/tests/test_problem_codes.py hold each library to this table.

codes.message: the block names no graph
codes.fix: start it with '// graph: <name>'

codes.message: the graph name '{name}' is not one word
codes.fix: use letters, digits and underscores only, such as reader_choice, not reader-choice

codes.message: a comment must be on a line of its own: // also occurs inside values, such as ni:/// hashes
codes.fix: put the comment on its own line

codes.message: cannot read '{text}'
codes.fix: a data block holds only things, links and plain values

codes.message: '{escape}' is not an escape GQL names
codes.fix: double the backslash to write a backslash: \{escape}

codes.message: the block is written in format {version}, newer than this reader, which reads format {reads}
codes.fix: read it with a newer reader: its text is kept as written

codes.message: expected '{expected}', found '{found}'
codes.fix: write '{expected}' here

codes.message: expected a name, found '{found}'
codes.fix: write a name here, in letters, digits and underscores

codes.message: '{text}' is not a date
codes.fix: write DATE 'YYYY-MM-DD'

codes.message: '{text}' is not an instant
codes.fix: write DATETIME 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+HH:MM'

codes.message: '{text}' has no offset
codes.fix: add its offset from UTC, such as +10:00

codes.message: '{text}' is not an instant: in UTC it falls outside years 1 to 9999
codes.fix: write DATETIME 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+HH:MM' within years 1 to 9999

codes.message: '{token}' is not a value a graph can hold
codes.fix: use 'text', a number, TRUE, FALSE, DATE '…' or DATETIME '…' — no lists, no expressions

codes.message: id {written} is not text
codes.fix: write id: {quoted} — a thing's id is always text

codes.message: SET would change {var}'s id, and a thing's id never changes
codes.fix: write the right thing, then link {var} to it or supersede it

codes.message: unexpected '{token}'
codes.fix: a data block ends after its INSERT and SET

codes.message: [{written}] has no colon, and graph {graph} has no relationship type called {written}
codes.fix: a relationship type is written with its colon: [:{type}]

codes.message: [{written}] has no colon, and graph {graph} has relationship types {types} and {last}, which differ only by case
codes.fix: write the one meant with its colon, such as [:{type}]

codes.message: this is a query block
codes.fix: queries ask questions of a graph; they are not data

codes.message: this is an excerpt
codes.fix: an excerpt illustrates part of a graph; it is not data

codes.message: MATCH must find a thing by its id alone
codes.fix: write MATCH (v:Label {id: '…'})

codes.message: MATCH finds no {labels} with id '{id}' in graph {graph}
codes.fix: the thing must be written earlier — in this document or one loaded before it

codes.message: {var} is written twice
codes.fix: give each new thing its own variable

codes.message: id '{id}' is already a thing in graph {graph}
codes.fix: an id names one thing — MATCH it to add to it, or supersede it

codes.message: {var} is used before it is written
codes.fix: write the thing before any link that uses it

codes.message: no thing called {var} in graph {graph}
codes.fix: check the spelling — or write it here with its kind: ({var}:Kind {…})

codes.message: SET names {var}, which is no thing in graph {graph}
codes.fix: check the spelling — SET names a thing by its id

codes.message: a target is named by its id alone
codes.fix: write MATCH (v:Kind {id: '…'}) — a thing by its name, a link by its two ends and its type

codes.message: a link is named by its type
codes.fix: write [r:TYPE] — a link by its two ends and its type

codes.message: a link is named by its two ends and its type alone
codes.fix: leave its values to a SET

codes.message: this names more than one target
codes.fix: a DELETE or SET names exactly one target

codes.message: {var} is not the one target
codes.fix: a DELETE or SET names exactly one target

codes.message: a DELETE needs the target it removes
codes.fix: write MATCH (v:Kind {id: '…'}) DELETE v

codes.message: DETACH is followed by DELETE
codes.fix: write DETACH DELETE v

codes.message: this removes more than one target
codes.fix: a DELETE or SET names exactly one target

codes.message: unexpected '{token}'
codes.fix: a DELETE ends after the one target it removes

codes.message: a link has no links to detach
codes.fix: write DELETE r

codes.message: a change is a DELETE or a SET
codes.fix: write DELETE or SET after the MATCH

codes.message: this changes more than one target
codes.fix: a DELETE or SET names exactly one target

codes.message: SET would change {var}'s id, and a thing's id never changes
codes.fix: write the right thing, then supersede it

codes.message: {key} is not a name a SET may give a value to
codes.fix: choose another name for the value

codes.message: unexpected '{token}'
codes.fix: a SET ends after its values

codes.message: the block names graph {named}, but the base gives it as graph {graph}
codes.fix: give it as graph {named} — a block is loaded into the graph its first line names

codes.message: id '{id}' is already a thing
codes.fix: an id names one thing — MATCH it to add to it, or supersede it

codes.message: cannot find where {var} is written
codes.fix: write it as (name:Kind {…})

codes.message: [{written}] has no colon
codes.fix: an engine is given only corrected text — read the block with its graph and load Store.corrected(block), or write it with its colon: [:{type}]

codes.message: the block is {size} characters long, over the limit of {limit}
codes.fix: split it into smaller graphs, each in its own block

codes.message: graph {graph} holds more than {limit} things and links
codes.fix: split it into smaller graphs that link to each other

codes.message: paths open into paths more than {limit} deep
codes.fix: give the paths fewer levels, at most {limit}

codes.message: a join of {count} documents is over the limit of {limit}
codes.fix: join at most {limit} documents at a time, then join the results

codes.message: the documents joined hold more than {limit} things and links
codes.fix: join fewer or smaller documents at a time
